title: Algebraic structures, homomorphisms, and substructures
fact_or_context_to_reference: Ring, integral-domain, field, and ordered-field laws; embeddings preserving constants, operations, and order. An operation- and constant-preserving map has a subalgebra as its image. The inverse of a bijective homomorphism preserves those operations and constants, including zero and one; an order-preserving field isomorphism and its inverse also preserve order. The current constructions supply their required laws locally. The canonical numeral map in a model of Robinson arithmetic preserves zero, successor, addition and multiplication; do not assume additional semiring laws for every such model.
